notes: P02 POPETS-X02_revocation_events deliverable: evaluation/venue2027/popets/revocation_model.py implements the exact target contract allowed(item, principal, purpose, time) -> TriDecision (ALLOW | DENY | INDETERMINATE) as a pure, injected-I/O gate over an append-only ConsentLedgerView (no hidden clock, no randomness, no network, no DB, no provider; synthetic principals/purposes only). PRECISE DISTINCTIONS (task core algorithm): (1) deletion of stored data is an ORTHOGONAL surface reported via stored_data_effect()/stored_data field ('deleted' at/after t_r, 'retained_unknown' before t_r or when provenance is unverifiable, 'not_applicable' under active consent or when no stored copy exists) and is never folded into the disclosure verdict; (2) prevention of future disclosure is the ONLY thing ALLOW/DENY speaks about (threat-model §2 predicate forbidden_label(g,p) ∩ lineage(d) = ∅ realized as consent-scope denial: every dispatch with time >= t_r in the revoked (principal, purpose|*) scope is DENY/DENY_POST_REVOCATION, boundary inclusive at t_r); (3) downstream already-delivered bytes are labeled OUT_OF_SCOPE_PAST (already_delivered_effect; threat-model §5.2, POPETS-CASE-06) — the verdict NEVER claims retroactive erasure of the delivered copy even while the platform-side stored copy is reported deleted, and with stored_copy=False no deletion is claimed at all; (4) model memorization is reported as memorization_guarantee='NOT_GUARANTEED' (machine unlearning is a different threat; novelty contract C2) — it is never converted into a DENY-as-erasure-guarantee (the post-revocation DENY reason code names the future-disclosure gate DENY_POST_REVOCATION, not unlearning) and it is attached to ALLOWED delivered items too. Explicit RevocationSemantics (revocation_semantics(), versioned 1.0.0, singleton, JSON-serializable) enumerates five guarantees (G1 future-disclosure prevention, G2 purpose boundary, G3 epoch-stale replay prevention on every transport, G4 stored-data deletion reported separately, G5 fail-closed INDETERMINATE) and four non-guarantees (N1 OUT_OF_SCOPE_PAST delivered bytes cannot be retracted, N2 memorization NOT_GUARANTEED, N3 no cryptographic retroactive erasure anywhere, N4 INDETERMINATE is first-class, never counted as safe rejection or completion). Determinations vs refusals: DENY_POST_REVOCATION (time >= t_r), DENY_EPOCH_STALE (payload bound to superseded consent epoch), PURPOSE_NOT_CONSENTED (known-but-unconsented purpose, POPETS-CASE-05), GRANT_UNKNOWN; INDETERMINATE refusals: PURPOSE_UNKNOWN (unknown purpose string fail closed), TIME_BEFORE_GRANT (clock before grant instant — the ledger timeline makes the query unevaluable; also covers backdated-grant overlap), LINEAGE_INDETERMINATE (missing or unverifiable lineage label, POPETS-CASE-07 fail-closed), PURPOSE_MISMATCH-free epoch vocabulary kept distinct from X06's fetch contract. Malformed item/principal/purpose/time raise ValueError with stable uppercase reason codes (ITEM_MALFORMED, PRINCIPAL_MALFORMED, PURPOSE_UNKNOWN, TIME_MALFORMED) — explicit refusals, never unhandled exceptions miscounted as safe rejections. test_revocation_events.py: 26 tests pass (positive: pre-revocation ALLOW with no deletion obligation, DENY at t_r inclusive and after for direct and transitive lineages, stored-data deletion flagged separately from the verdict on the same instant, wildcard purpose revocation coverage, stale epoch replay DENY, unconsented-purpose DENY, no-grant DENY, explicit semantics promises/non-promises, JSON round-trips incl. model_version passthrough, determinism, mapping-shaped ledger acceptance; adversarial: already-delivered bytes NOT claimed deleted (OUT_OF_SCOPE_PAST marker, no erasure reason code, platform-copy deletion reported only in its own field, no deletion claim when stored_copy=False), memorization NOT_GUARANTEED on both DENY and ALLOW paths never as erasure claim, unknown purpose refused INDETERMINATE + blank purpose refused, clock before grant refused INDETERMINATE incl. t=0, missing/None lineage label fail-closed INDETERMINATE, 8 malformed-input stable-code refusals, INDETERMINATE first-class (never coerced), future-effective revocation applies exactly at revoked_at, backdated-grant overlap refused and cannot resurrect the revoked scope, emergency-override purpose string cannot bypass the gate).
